rows.Title: Unit 1 · Still Life
Research of one still life artist and analysis of tone, composition and media, planning own still life arrangement, experimenting with background options, recording findings in journals
Introduction to colour theory (complementary, analogous, limited palette), colour studies to enhance form and depth, blending and layering exercises, group critique

Introduction to composition principles (rule of thirds, balance, overlapping), using viewfinders to explore arrangement, photography of still life with varied backdrops, sketching thumbnails of compositions
Learners decide on final arrangement and medium, begin sustained drawing or painting, teacher feedback during progress, recording reasoning in journals
Demonstration of alternative media (oil pastel, ink, collage), experimental studies using chosen arrangement in different media, reflection on effects of media, annotation of experiments in journals
Introduction to the unit and objectives, discussion on still life, presentation of artist examples (Cézanne, Morandi), quick observational sketches, reflection and annotation in journals
Demonstration of shading techniques (hatching, cross-hatching, blending), tonal studies from single object, practice rendering form through tone, peer review and annotation
Unit 2 · Identity
Select final composition and media. Start sustained study, with teacher feedback and ongoing reflection in journals
Completion of sustained study, peer critique and self-reflection, annotation and evaluation of final piece, discussion of how skills support future units
Finalise sustained outcome. Group critique, peer feedback and self-evaluation recorded in journals
Select one artist for inspiration. Explore composition and formal elements. Produce two different possible compositions for final piece
Discussion of "Identity" and brainstorming (portraiture, objects, heritage, family, environment). Presentation of diverse artist examples. Vocabulary: composition, representation, heritage
Experiment with a variety of media (paint, pastel, collage, mixed media) to explore expression of identity. Annotate and reflect in journals
Drawing and photography of objects and faces linked to identity. Annotation of initial ideas. Connections to still life and self-portraiture
Develop two chosen compositions further (e.g. portrait vs. object focus). Annotate strengths, weaknesses and potential for final outcome
Unit 3 · On the Surface
Research and analyse one artist related to chosen theme. Visual journal annotations and small experimental response
Research and analyse one chosen artist related to identity. Record visual notes and create a small experimental study inspired by the artist
Finalise outcome. Group critique, peer feedback and self-evaluation recorded in journals
Select one or two artists for inspiration. Produce exploratory sketches and mixed media responses
Create two different possible compositions for a final outcome. Focus on composition, contrast and expression
Begin sustained final piece using chosen media and composition. Teacher guidance and peer feedback
Continue sustained final outcome. Layering, texture, refinement
Group discussion of “On the Surface”. Presentation of artist examples. Vocabulary: texture, layer, contrast, representation
Explore pencil and paint to investigate texture, pattern and layering effects
Explore collage, mixed media, and printmaking. Annotate reflections in journal
Evaluate strengths/weaknesses of two compositions. Select final direction and refine design through studies
Brainstorming sketches and quick observational drawings. Collection of images/photography connected to the theme
Unit 4 · Exhibition
Plan layout of exhibition space (library/hall/classroom). Small groups mount/display work, considering audience and communication
Learners refine and mount chosen works. Consider order, flow, and visual impact. Teacher feedback on editing and selection
Exhibition to peers/guests. Learners present their work and explain choices. Group critique and self-reflection in journals
Discuss purpose of exhibition. Vocabulary: presentation, selection, editing, audience. Learners review all their work from Units 9.1–9.3 and begin selecting final outcome + 3 supporting sheets
